case: a phrase search ran over a line cut to 220 characters and reported the phrase absent
provenance: Failure 2 of the four. A seat grepped a file for a phrase, saw no match, and concluded the phrase was absent; its pipeline piped through `cut -c1-220`, so it had searched a truncation of a one-paragraph line, and reading the file whole reversed the conclusion. The shape is reconstructed here against this repository's own CLAUDE.md, whose line 14 is 1,127 characters of one paragraph: `never an amend` sits past character 220, the truncated search finds nothing, and the same search over the whole line returns 1. Run in this worktree on 2026-09-23.
command: sed -n '14p' CLAUDE.md | cut -c1-220 | grep -n "never an amend"
